scope: sampled visual and story review; ASR and measured signal support; no validated audio listening
product_from_film: Project Genie is presented as a research prototype for creating, remixing and exploring playable worlds from text and images.
explains_well: The alpine meadow example shows separate environment and character prompts, a sketch, a create-world action and movement through the resulting scene.
unclear: The edit skips generation waits and gives no clear limits on session length, control reliability or persistent world behavior.
scenario: Create an alpine world with a dog, remix the character, then turn personal images into explorable scenes.
product_clear_basis: Environment and character prompt fields begin the full creation example after the research-prototype introduction.

scenes.action: Small world clips surround text introducing Genie 3. A circular image becomes a paper-plane world, then joins a field of circular worlds under Project Genie and research-prototype text.
scenes.design: Black background, white titles and circular scene windows.
scenes.purpose: Introduce the model history and the playable-world concept.
scenes.evidence: Visible chronological 1 fps samples, source 0–26s; boundary approximate; exact motion between samples unverified.

scenes.action: A curved grid workspace shows environment and character fields. Text requests an alpine meadow with a cabin and a Shiba Inu. Create sketch produces a matching still, then Create world leads through a blurred transition.
scenes.design: Dark prompt interface and a bright alpine preview.
scenes.evidence: Visible chronological 1 fps samples, source 26–39s; boundary approximate; exact motion between samples unverified.

scenes.action: The dog moves through the meadow toward the cabin and later across grass near a fence. A person at the monitor and keyboard is intercut with the world view.
scenes.design: Third-person view with small input indicators and physical keyboard footage.
scenes.purpose: Show exploration of the created scene.
scenes.evidence: Visible chronological 1 fps samples, source 39–50s; boundary approximate; exact motion between samples unverified.

scenes.action: Remix your world introduces a request to change the character to a pink balloon rabbit. The rabbit appears in the meadow, then in a bouncy-house setting, treehouse and watercolor-style landscape.
scenes.design: Prompt close-up followed by varied worlds retaining the pink character.
scenes.evidence: Visible chronological 1 fps samples, source 50–61s; boundary approximate; exact motion between samples unverified.

scenes.action: A climber, ant, flying bird and small character on a pool table illustrate different perspectives. A blue-ball prompt is followed by a ball leaving a blue trail across white terrain. A wingsuit scene and flashlight-lit animal follow.
scenes.design: Varied generated environments and recurring control indicators.
scenes.purpose: Broaden the range of characters and interactions.
scenes.evidence: Visible chronological 1 fps samples, source 61–85s; boundary approximate; exact motion between samples unverified.

scenes.action: Hands build a small cardboard figure and photograph it on a workbench. The image enters a world-creation interface; the figure then walks across a matching workshop tabletop among objects.
scenes.design: Physical making and phone capture lead to a generated third-person scene.
scenes.purpose: Show an image becoming a playable starting point.
scenes.evidence: Visible chronological 1 fps samples, source 85–98s; boundary approximate; exact motion between samples unverified.

scenes.action: A person photographs a cat in a living room. A still preview gives way to a cat moving across the sofa toward the window and cat tree.
scenes.design: Phone capture followed by a recognizable room and cat view.
scenes.purpose: Repeat the image-to-world idea with a familiar personal subject.
scenes.evidence: Visible chronological 1 fps samples, source 98–110s; boundary approximate; exact motion between samples unverified.

scenes.action: A portrait is attached to an image prompt requesting an early-2000s low-poly character. The result becomes a moving figure in a glowing forest, then joins a grid of different people and visual styles.
scenes.design: Image-generation prompt, low-poly scene and multiplying character tiles.
scenes.purpose: Show a stylized personal character and extend the range of examples.
scenes.evidence: Visible chronological 1 fps samples, source 110–124s; boundary approximate; exact motion between samples unverified.

scenes.action: Motorcycle, playground and space-car examples carry Imagine worlds, Create worlds and Play worlds. Circular scenes return, then the film ends with labs.google/ProjectGenie.
scenes.design: World montage, circular gallery and a long readable URL card.
scenes.purpose: Summarize the invitation and provide a destination.
scenes.evidence: Visible chronological 1 fps samples, source 124–138.888s; boundary approximate; exact motion between samples unverified.

lessons.keep: Show a recognizable physical input becoming an explorable result.
lessons.avoid: Avoid letting short varied examples imply unlimited persistence or precise control.
lessons.open: Generation time, control latency, session limits, long-term continuity, physics behavior and all audio properties remain unverified.
try: For Tin, carry one handmade or user-supplied asset from capture through creation to output.
Keep one interaction uncut with the input and response visible together.

comparison.story: Introduce the model history and the playable-world concept. → Explain the two-stage creation flow. → Show exploration of the created scene. → Show character and environment remixing. → Broaden the range of characters and interactions. → Show an image becoming a playable starting point. → Repeat the image-to-world idea with a familiar personal subject. → Show a stylized personal character and extend the range of examples. → Summarize the invitation and provide a destination.
comparison.motion: Circular world windows gather around titles, prompt text fills fields, still previews blur into moving scenes, characters travel through environments, a blue ball leaves a trail and portrait examples multiply into a grid. Sampling scope: 1 fps unless a closer window is recorded.
